text: Agreed to pace rolling endurance rides steadily on climbs without surging, using conversational breathing and comfortable cadence to control effort.
The final riser felt unusually hard, but it was ridden into a headwind after a long day on the athlete’s feet; this was judged situational rather than evidence of declining fitness.
For exposed headwinds, agreed to use a lower bar position and move snacks earlier to preserve final-hour energy, while monitoring hand and shoulder comfort as volume increases.
Mild leg heaviness on day two of back-to-back rides cleared after 20 minutes of easy spinning, so the plan remained unchanged.
Agreed that if second-day leg heaviness ever lasts beyond 30 minutes, the ride will be shortened rather than completed at the risk of digging a fatigue hole.
For rides over two hours, agreed on one bottle per hour, food every 30 minutes, and a larger breakfast before sustained climbing; the routine will be practiced first on easy rides.
The park-side recovery route with fewer junctions allowed relaxed breathing throughout and made genuinely easy effort easier to maintain.
Recovery spins will start from the park side of town going forward, and easy days will be protected even when the schedule becomes busy.
